why: Three bugs shipped behind a green suite because each JS suite hand-built its own
partial version of this response. One fixture put the human name in `name`, so 30
tests passed over a screen of raw ability ids; another left `enabled` out, so
filtering on it silently dropped an agent's cards; another left `icon` out, so
dashicon slugs rendered as literal text. Every one was found by looking at the
screen. This file is the one description of the response shape: the PHP schema is
pinned to it, the real endpoint's output is pinned to it, and the JS fixture
builder is generated from it, so a fixture that drifts fails a test instead of
`presence` is the rule for when the endpoint emits a key, not permission for a
fixture to omit it. See the JS fixture builder for which variant carries which.

presenceRules.always: Emitted for every ability in every response. A fixture may never omit one.
presenceRules.ability_subclass: Emitted only for a `VIPWorkflows\Abilities\Ability`, which a plain `WP_Ability` is not. Every VIP agent is one, so the default fixture variant carries these; only the deliberate plain-ability variant omits them.
presenceRules.request_param: Emitted only when a request parameter asks for it. Absent from the default variant, because the default models a request that did not pass that parameter.

id.why: The ability identifier. Same value as `name`.

name.why: `WP_Ability::get_name()` — the ability *identifier*, not a human name. This is the key the label bug got wrong.

label.why: The human-readable name. The only key safe to render to a reader.

meta.why: Ability meta. `supports`, `stage_eligible` and `transition_eligible` are read off it to filter by context.

enabled.why: Whether the agent may be run. The endpoint does NOT filter turned-off agents out, so a consumer that filters on this key needs it present on every fixture to be tested at all.

show_in_commands.why: Whether the tool appears in the editor command palette.

availability.why: Serialized availability. A plain `WP_Ability` has no structured channel, so it serializes the empty "nothing unmet" result rather than omitting the key — a consumer never branches on presence.

check_modes.why: Per-ability check modes from settings, merged onto every row after the collect loop.

icon.why: A dashicon slug (`search`) or a literal glyph. Rendering the slug as text is what the icon bug looked like on screen.

required_for.why: Transitions that require this tool. Added only when `post_id` is passed, which also narrows the collection to required tools.

identityKeys.why: Both carry the ability identifier and are built from the same `get_name()` call, so they can never disagree. A fixture where they differ is describing a response no endpoint returns.

invariants.abilityIdPatternWhy: Ability names are `namespace/slug`. A human name like `Web Researcher` cannot match, which is what makes the label-in-`name` bug detectable rather than a matter of taste.

labelKeys.why: Must not equal the identifier. A fixture whose label IS the id cannot distinguish a component that renders the label from one that renders the raw id — which is the bug.
